panels.title: Scrape targets up
panels.description: json_exporter has NO probe_success metric. A fetch failure returns HTTP 503 and a config fault panics the handler; in both cases NO samples are ingested at all. `up` is the ONLY signal that a number on this dashboard is stale rather than real. Expect 4 targets.

panels.title: Cost coverage · active provider groups
panels.description: One means every provider group with real requests resolved to the current pricing table. Empty scopes are excluded because the plugin reports zero coverage both for no traffic and for unpriced traffic.

panels.title: Per-model reconciliation
panels.description: Self-audit. sum(per-model requests) / sum(scope totals) should sit at 1.00. It drifts below 1.00 exactly when the summary API's `limit` parameter has truncated models[] - otherwise a completely silent form of undercounting.

panels.title: Credentials in error/disabled
panels.description: Credentials whose status is error or disabled. A DELETED credential vanishes from the API entirely, so its row disappears rather than showing an error state.

panels.title: Lifetime cost · selected providers
panels.description: Lifetime model-level estimate for the selected providers. The reconciliation health tile must remain at 1.0 for this model sum to be complete.

panels.title: Estimated cost by model · $usage_window
panels.description: Plugin-computed window values filtered by the Usage window and Provider controls. The 20m last-over-time range covers the deliberately slow 15m scrape of 30d aggregates. No rate() is used because pricing refreshes can move estimates down.

panels.title: Estimated cost · $usage_window
panels.description: Model-level plugin aggregate for exactly one selected window. This previously summed the 24h and 30d series and therefore overstated the result.

panels.title: Estimated cost by provider · $usage_window
panels.description: Provider comparison from model-level aggregates, so Claude, Codex, and future providers share the same path and scope=other is never treated as a provider.

panels.title: Token mix by provider
panels.description: Counter rates grouped by real provider labels. Cache-read dominance is useful for Claude Code, while Codex reasoning and output remain separately visible.

panels.title: Lifetime usage by provider
panels.description: Requests, tokens, and estimated cost use the same per-model source for every provider. Claude per-credential token and cost attribution is not exposed.

panels.title: Request rate by credential
panels.description: Failures plotted negative. These counters are in-memory in cliproxy and reset to 0 on pod restart - correct counter semantics, handled by rate(). success+failed is NOT a lifetime total.

panels.title: Failure ratio by credential

targets.expr: sum by (provider, email) (rate(cliproxy_auth_requests_failed_total{provider=~"${provider:regex}"}[15m])) / clamp_min(sum by (provider, email) (rate(cliproxy_auth_requests_success_total{provider=~"${provider:regex}"}[15m]) + rate(cliproxy_auth_requests_failed_total{provider=~"${provider:regex}"}[15m])), 0.001)

panels.description: The clamp_min is load-bearing: without it an idle credential gives 0/0 = NaN and the panel flickers to garbage.

panels.title: Credential health
panels.description: A credential that is deleted (or runtime-only and disabled) is OMITTED from the API response entirely, so its row DISAPPEARS rather than showing an error state. Absence is the failure mode to watch.

panels.title: Provider-group latency / TTFT · $usage_window
panels.description: Window means, not quantiles. The upstream summary exposes only scope here: codex, other, and xai. 'other' can contain Claude, Gemini, or future providers, so this panel deliberately does not relabel it as Claude or obey Provider filtering.

panels.title: Slow requests · $usage_window
panels.description: Provider-group values because the upstream summary exposes only scope. Thresholds are fixed upstream: latency >= 12s and TTFT >= 3s.

panels.title: Rate limits by provider group
panels.description: Counter rate by upstream scope. The current API does not expose Codex and non-Codex rate limits through one shared provider-labelled metric.

panels.title: Failed requests by provider group
panels.description: Counter rate by upstream scope. 'other' remains explicit because it may aggregate Claude, Gemini, and future providers.

panels.title: Output tokens/sec by provider group · $usage_window
panels.description: The plugin publishes this only by scope, not real provider label; 'other' is therefore kept explicit and may aggregate multiple non-Codex providers.

panels.title: Claude quota used
panels.description: Bounded utilization reported by Anthropic's OAuth usage API. Missing windows remain No Data; traffic token counters are never used to estimate quota.

panels.title: Claude quota remaining
panels.description: 100 minus Anthropic's explicitly reported, bounded utilization percentage; not inferred from token usage.

panels.title: Claude quota reset
panels.description: Reset timestamps reported by Anthropic; absent when upstream omits them.

panels.title: Codex quota used (primary)
panels.description:
CODEX ACCOUNTS ONLY. These fields are omitempty and are genuinely ABSENT for non-Codex credentials, so this panel shows No Data when no Codex account is registered.

AN EMPTY PANEL DOES NOT MEAN QUOTA IS FINE - it means the field was not reported. `or vector(0)` is deliberately NOT used here: it would append a phantom 0% gauge that reads as healthy. Cross-check the credential health table.

panels.title: Codex secondary quota remaining
panels.description: Plugin-side estimate, Codex accounts only.

panels.title: Per-account usage (Codex only)
panels.description: The plugin exposes account token/cost/quota fields only for Codex. Claude and other provider credentials still appear in the provider-neutral auth panels, but missing per-account usage must not be interpreted as zero.

title: CLIProxyAPI / Usage & cost
description: Provider-neutral operational usage for every model routed through CLIProxyAPI. The Usage window variable selects plugin-computed 24h or 30d aggregates; Grafana's time picker controls counter-rate panels. Costs are pricing-table estimates, not provider invoices.
